messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — I pushed a small prototype for an 'Authz Coach' in console. It walks admins through creating a role with scoped routes, shows a preview of routing policies applied, and gives a rough quota/cost delta. Want quick feedback before I link the mock.
Jon: Nice. Is this aimed at new tenants or existing enterprise admins who manage many roles?
Maya: Both. Flow detects if there are existing role templates and suggests a 'narrower' role. For enterprise, it surfaces SSO group mappings and whether the role will block any current service accounts. Trying to avoid surprises.
Sara: How are you computing the quota/cost delta? That part worries me — we need to avoid misleading numbers.
Maya: Right — current impl uses historical per-route token rates + model profile to estimate. It's intentionally conservative: shows a range (low/median/high) and flags estimates that rely on sparse telemetry.
Eli: Can we show which requests contributed to the estimate? A sample query list would help admins decide.
Maya: Yep, there's a "why this estimate" panel that links to the last 7d sample and a compact histogram. But it's gated by tenant telemetry settings (PII-safe).
Jon: API-wise, what endpoints are you adding? I want something server-side so CLI and infra teams can reuse it.
Maya: Added two endpoints:

1) `POST /v1/console/authz/preview` — payload: role spec + optional tenant_id + window
2) `GET /v1/console/authz/samples?role_id=...` — returns sampled request signatures

Will add authz-scoped rate limiting on both.
Sara: We should not leak exact request payloads. The samples must be redacted and only include route, model, token_count, anonymized tenant-id.
Eli: Also consider impersonation: if an admin creates a role that grants service-account:impersonate, the coach should surface cascade effects (e.g., this role enables full access via downstream services).
Maya: Good call — plan to show a chain visualization and flag any impersonation perms with high severity.
Jon: Rollout plan? feature flag + gradual expose to small subset of orgs? We need crash-safe fallback if the preview API is slow.
Maya: Flagged behind `authz_coach` feature flag. Start with 5% of new tenants, then internal beta orgs, then wider. Also a fallback: if preview takes >2s, show a lightweight heuristic + CTA "try again later".
Sara: Telemetry: we need events for preview_opened, preview_submitted, estimate_accepted, estimate_rejected, and sample_viewed. Should capture feature_flag, role_template_used, and severity_flags.
Eli: Add event for "blocked_binding_detected" when the generated role would immediately block existing service accounts — important for rollout telemetry.
Maya: Agree. Also adding a sparse sampling option so we don't store full details for long. Retention 7d by default, configurable for enterprise.
Jon: One more: console UX copy. People misunderstand "scope" vs "route" a lot. Coach should use plain language: "what this role can do" and show examples like `Can generate text with model:x for route /inference/chat`.
Maya: Working with UX on microcopy. Also inline links to docs and a "simulate" button that simulates a request using the preview (no live tokens consumed).
Sara: For enterprise controls, we need an admin override and audit log entry whenever the coach suggests narrowing but admin chooses broad role.
Maya: Already planned: every creation via coach creates an audit log with suggestion delta. Also a diff view for later rollback.
Eli: Security review note: block the coach from proposing roles that include `root:*` or other dangerous wildcards. We should auto-rewrite to a safer pattern and explain the change.
Maya: Implemented an auto-normalizer with reason codes.
deploy-bot: maya/authz-coach-preview deployed to staging at maya-coach-20240306-01 — visit https://staging.console/redwood/coach (password: team-only)
Jon: I'll run the infra integration tests tomorrow and exercise the CLI endpoints.
Sara: I'll draft the telemetry event spec and send a short PR for microcopy.
Eli: I'll do a quick security pass on the wildcard normalizer.
Maya: Thanks all. If you have specific edge case requests drop them here or ping me @Maya. Planning a short demo next Tue.
Jon: +1 to demo. :thumbsup:
